API stability — flexyBayes

Source: API_STABILITY.md

flexyBayes is in the 0.3.x series. Every public export carries a lifecycle::badge("experimental"). The stability guarantees below are therefore deliberately weaker than they will be at v1.0.

Stability ladder (lifecycle)

Stage Meaning for flexyBayes
stable Behaviour and signature frozen across the 1.x series; breaking changes ride a major version bump and a deprecation cycle. No exports are stable yet.
maturing Behaviour and signature unlikely to change in 0.x; minor signature additions are non-breaking.
experimental Behaviour and signature may change in any 0.x release. Bug fixes and additions never break, but renamings, default-value changes, and shape changes are allowed with a lifecycle::deprecate_warn() cycle of at least one minor release. All v0.3.x exports.
deprecated Function still callable; emits lifecycle::deprecate_warn(). Removal scheduled per NEWS.md.
superseded Function still callable, no warning, but a newer entry point is preferred.

Per-export stability surface (v0.3.x)

The four-verb spine plus its companion diagnostics:

Export Stage Notes
flexybayes() experimental ASReml-style entry (fixed, random, rcov). backend = c("greta", "inla", "auto"). prior argument accepts fb_prior().
fb_brms() experimental brms / lme4-style entry. backend = c("greta", "inla", "brms", "auto"); "brms" is the Stan passthrough via brms::brm(). "auto" never routes to Stan (Decision 8 in ADR 0015).
fb_greta() experimental Expert direct-greta entry. Accepts a user-built greta model; prior is declaration-only (the user’s graph is not re-priored).
fb() experimental Literal alias for flexybayes(); documented but not promoted.
triangulate() experimental Pairwise cross-engine posterior comparison. Metric set fixed for 0.3.x (Wasserstein-1, R-hat-on-means, tail drift, SD ratio, mean difference). Additions are non-breaking; metric removals or renamings ride a deprecation cycle.
fb_prior() experimental PC-canonical hybrid prior DSL on the SD scale. Supported targets: sigma, sd(group), b(name), cor(group), smooth(var). Supported families: pc, normal, student_t, half_normal, half_cauchy, cauchy, gamma, exponential, lkj, uniform.
prior_summary() experimental S3 generic returning the resolved-prior view for a fit. Methods registered for flexybayes, flexybayes_inla, flexybayes_brms, and flexybayes_direct_greta.
backend_decision() experimental Returns the captured dispatch trace (backend, path, gate_checks, reason). Shape stable across 0.3.x.
canonical_names() experimental S3 generic returning the canonical-name registry view for a fit. Methods registered for all four fit subclasses.
proceed(), cat_code() experimental Review-code workflow companions for review_code = TRUE fits.
fb_as_draws_simple() experimental S3 generic; methods for all four fit subclasses. Returns a named list of named draw vectors.
tidy.flexybayes(), glance.flexybayes(), augment.flexybayes() experimental broom-compliant; column names follow broom convention and are stable for the columns currently emitted. New columns are non-breaking.
recover_data.flexybayes(), emm_basis.flexybayes() experimental emmeans-compliant; signatures dictated by the emmeans S3 contract.
print.lgm_refusal() experimental Internal S3 method, registered for dispatch only; output format may evolve when ADR 0017 lands (refusal sites consolidated into lgm_gate()).
predict.flexybayes() (Stage 3A / 3B) experimental newdata interface mirrors stats::predict(); v0.3.5 added output_file / format = c("auto","csv","rds","fst") / interop arguments + allow_new_levels = c("population","sample","refuse"). Interval semantics are posterior expected-response, not posterior-predictive (no residual observation noise). Stage 3A $aggregate argument is backend-asymmetric: "auto" activates the aggregated path on backend = "inla"; on backend = "greta" requires explicit TRUE.
Known-covariance carriers on vm() / ped() (Stage 5A) experimental v0.3.7: chol = L (greta only), precision = Q (greta + INLA via generic0), ped(..., use_sparse_precision = TRUE). Mutually exclusive with the dense V carrier and with each other. blocks = list(V1, V2, ...) reserves its input vocabulary in v0.3.7 and refuses with route_not_yet_emitted (lands v0.3.8). low_rank_factor = reserves a slot gated behind ADR 0027 (Stage 6 / v0.4.0); refuses with approximate_route_not_yet_registered.

Internal-but-S3-visible diagnostics

A small set of internal constructors – .fb_dataset(), .fb_preflight(), .fb_aggregate_gaussian(), .fb_aggregation_plan() – are not exported, but their S3 print / format methods are registered for dispatch on diagnostic output (refusal messages, review_code summaries, interactive inspection at the console). Because the methods are registered via the S3 mechanism, R CMD check requires generated .Rd entries; those entries are visible from ?print.fb_preflight and similar.

Stability promise for these methods through 0.3.x:

  • The methods exist and dispatch correctly on instances of the internal classes.
  • The output format – column ordering, whitespace, exact wording – is internal-grade and may change without a deprecation cycle.
  • Programmatic use is not supported: parse the structured slot fields on the underlying object ($per_term_estimate, $sufficient_stats, $dictionaries, etc.) rather than the printed string.

The constructor functions themselves remain internal. Stable export is gated on at least two downstream workflows (Stage 3A aggregation in v0.3.2; Stage 3B chunked predict in v0.3.3) reaching the contract stability bar.

Default-value contract (v0.3.x)

The current prior contract on the auto-default path — that is, when neither a user fb_prior() nor a legacy prior_vc_sd scalar is supplied:

Target Default Reference
Residual sigma (Gaussian, identity link) uniform(0, 5 * sd(y)) Gelman 2006
Residual sigma (log link) uniform(0, 5 * sd(log(y + 0.5))) Gelman 2006
Residual sigma (logit link) uniform(0, 5) Gelman 2006
sd(group) for simple / ide / id random terms uniform(0, U) with U set as above by family Gelman 2006
sd(group) for vm(), ped() structured-cov terms uniform(0, U) with U set by family (matches the random-intercept default; routes via .sigma_decl()) Gelman 2006
sd(group) for at(), us(), fa(), ar1(), spl() structured-cov terms legacy lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) — per-form uniform default deferred to a future minor release flexyBayes legacy
Fixed-effect coefficients (intercept, slopes, factor contrasts, I() expressions) normal(0, prior_fixed_sd) with prior_fixed_sd = 100 Gelman 2006

The PC prior remains a first-class explicit option via fb_prior(sigma ~ pc(upper = U, prob = p)), and is the cross-engine interlingua (Simpson et al. 2017) for translation across greta / INLA / brms. It is no longer the auto-default; the auto-default is the bounded uniform on SD.

The legacy scalar bridge (prior_fixed_sd, prior_vc_sd) preserves the original lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) semantics verbatim when the caller passes prior_vc_sd explicitly. prior_summary() reports which of the three resolution paths fired (auto-default, user-supplied, legacy-scalar).

The prior_fixed_sd default raised from 10 to 100 between the local 2026-04-27 rename and the v0.2 finalisation, per ADR 0010 — the previous value was too tight for responses on the natural data scale (e.g., sleepstudy$Reaction with mean ≈ 298 ms) and induced a substantial intercept bias against the REML reference.

Deprecation policy

When an experimental export is renamed, restructured, or removed:

  1. The old call path emits lifecycle::deprecate_warn() for at least one minor release (a “warn cycle”).
  2. The next minor release moves the old call path to lifecycle::deprecate_stop() (“error cycle”); the function still exists but signals a hard error directing callers to the replacement.
  3. The next minor release after that removes the old export entirely.

For a default-value change, the old default remains available behind an explicit argument for at least the entire 0.x series.

Compatibility commitments through 0.3.x

Stable across the 0.3.x patch line:

  • The four fit subclasses’ externally-visible top-level structure ($glm, plus the backend-specific slot: $greta, $inla, or $brms, plus $extras).
  • The fb_prior() print method’s output format.
  • The triangulate() return shape — metrics data frame columns, common / only_a / only_b character vectors, n_common scalar, source_a / source_b strings.
  • The backend_decision() return shape — backend, path, gate_checks, reason.
  • The prior_summary() return shape — kind, backend, default_origin, fb_prior, default_scale, default_basis, declaration_only.

What changes when

Change class Where it can land
New parameter with default value any patch (0.3.0.9001)
New behaviour behind opt-in argument any patch
Bug fix that changes numerical output within tolerance any patch — flagged in NEWS.md
New exported function minor (0.4.0)
Renamed export with deprecation cycle minor
Removed export (post-deprecation cycle) minor
Class-structure change minor
Backend swap (e.g., greta → gretaR) at the flexybayes() level minor; gated by capability detection so calls keep working

Pinning

Production users who need stability should pin to a specific 0.3.x patch via renv::snapshot() until v1.0 lands.

Roadmap to v1.0

  • v0.2.5 — hardening: fold emit_inla() refusals into lgm_gate() (ADR 0017); smooth-basis retention on the IR for predict() with newdata (ADR 0018); structured-covariance default priors extend ADR 0004; numerical-snapshot plot regression tests replacing the vdiffr skip.
  • v0.3 — Ambition lane: triangulate_all() over fitted-model lists; tensor smooths (te / ti / t2); BYM2 spatial random effects; NIMBLE HMM proof; PESTO → prior bridge (ADR 0008); posteriordb ≥40-paired test corpus; gretaR slot activation (external precondition).
  • v0.4 — survival (parametric AFT + Cox via INLA Poisson); multi-engine missing-data ensemble.
  • v0.9 — release rehearsal; lift exports from experimental to maturing; freeze API for v1.0.
  • v1.0 — promote core exports to stable.
